cards.text: This is a psalm of David, Israel's king, and friend, he SKIPS the small talk. No 'hello,' no 'how's Your week.' The first words out of his mouth to the LORD are: "How long, O LORD?"

cards.question: David opens by asking the LORD, "How long, O LORD?" What does he ask the LORD right after that?

answers.text: Whether God will forget him forever
Whether God will send rain soon
Whether God will make him rich

cards.text: Then he asks how long the LORD will hide His face, and how long he has to wrestle in his soul with sorrow in his heart each day. EACH DAY, friend, not one rough Monday but the WHOLE CALENDAR.

cards.question: I bet God feels far away to David, but he's got trouble down here too. He asks how long someone will dominate him. Who is it?

cards.text: Then the questions stop, and David asks for something instead: "Consider me and respond, O LORD my God." And he wants God to give light to his eyes.

cards.question: David says that if the LORD doesn't give light to his eyes, he could sleep in death.

cards.text: And David's not done. If he goes down, there's something else that could happen, and it's about his enemy.

cards.question: David says that if he falls, his foes will mourn for him.

cards.text: His enemy would get to say, "I have overcome him," and his foes would cheer. Being down is hard, and I think having someone cheer about it is harder.
Then David drops one little word. Real quiet. ... But.

cards.question: After all those "how long" questions, what does David say he has trusted in?
David's done asking how long. He says his ___ will rejoice in the LORD's salvation.

cards.text: Then David says he will sing to the LORD. Five verses ago this man was asking if God forgot him, and now he's WARMING UP HIS VOICE!

cards.question: David says he will sing to the LORD. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD has been good to him
His enemy has finally run off
